entries.reason: Local-development trust boundary: exposes the developer's whole ~/.ssh (private keys) to everything running in the container, so git can push over SSH. Never use this container for untrusted code.
Local-development trust boundary: exposes the developer's whole ~/.gnupg (secret keyring) read-write to the container so commits/tags can be GPG-signed (repo requires signing).
Persists shell history in the workspace (git-ignored). Low risk: single file inside the workspace, but history can contain pasted secrets.
Local-development trust boundary: shares Claude Code config, history and credentials from the host with the container so login persists across rebuilds.
Local-development trust boundary: shares the Claude Code account/state file (may contain OAuth details) from the host with the container.

Local-development trust boundary: shares the host's Codex CLI config and credentials (~/.codex, incl. auth tokens) read-write with the container so login and settings sync across devices like ~/.claude. Everything running in the container can read the token.
Local-development trust boundary: disables the default seccomp filter, widening the container-escape surface. Kept for tooling that needs blocked syscalls; revisit and drop if no longer required.
Runs on the HOST before the container starts (outside the sandbox). Only creates the directories/files that the bind mounts above need, so Docker does not create them as root.

Local-development trust boundary: gives the container a docker CLI wired to the HOST Docker daemon. Anything in the container can start privileged containers on the host, i.e. it is equivalent to root on the host.
